subject: Clarify: billable token definition, streaming session window & smoothing for committed tiers

Subject: Clarify metrics for committed discount tiers and streaming sessions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the overview on Monday — the team and I are reviewing the term sheet. A couple of precise metric questions came up from procurement and engineering that we need clarified before legal proceeds:

1) Billable token definition: are billable tokens defined as the sum of client-side prompt tokens + model-generated tokens, or are there any deductions (e.g., prefix cached tokens, deterministic system tokens)? We need explicit language for the SOW.

2) Streaming sessions: we do a lot of long-lived streams (incremental user messages + streaming assistant tokens). How does Redwood meter streaming tokens? Is it per-token, or do you use a session windowing approach where short idle periods get smoothed?

3) Rounding and committable buckets: the term sheet references "commit tiers" and a monthly smoothing/consolidation. How is rounding handled on streaming: per-token, per-second, or per-stream? We need examples for our finance team (e.g., 1.2M tokens streamed across 10k sessions — how will that be counted against the commit?).

Finally, procurement wants to confirm whether unused commit can be carried forward or smoothed into next period if usage volatility spikes.

Can you provide suggested contract language and a worked example we can attach to our purchase order?

Best,
Jamie
Procurement, Acme Enterprises

Jamie — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full language and examples below:

- Billable tokens = client prompt tokens + model-generated tokens minus tokens that hit an explicit prefix cache entry (we don’t count locally cached prefixes if the cache is at the request router and eliminates generation). System prompts and deterministic routing tokens are included unless explicitly excluded by a customer-managed cache policy.

- Streaming is metered by token, but we apply an optional session-window smoothing for customers on commits to reduce volatility. The smoothing groups short-lived idle gaps (< 30s by default) inside a session; tokens are still counted, but the billing window can be rounded to a configurable quantum (e.g., 1 second or 1 token) depending on the contract.

- Rounding defaults: per-token for everyone; for commit tiers we can offer per-second rounding as an alternative for streaming-heavy customers to avoid micro-token noise. Carry-forward (true-up vs carry-forward) is negotiable — by default we do a 30-day smoothing window for committed customers, with a one-time carry-forward up to 10% of monthly commit if you purchase an annual commit.

I'll attach draft clause language and a worked example in the next email.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jamie — looping back with the draft language and worked example. I've included both a standard meter and streaming-friendly meter so you can pick:

--- DRAFT CLAUSE A: Standard per-token meter (default) ---
Billable Unit: For purposes of this Agreement, a "Billable Token" means any input token supplied to Redwood's API (including user prompts, system messages, and any other input data) together with any output token generated by the model in response. Tokens which are fully satisfied by an explicit Redwood-managed prefix cache (where no model generation is required) shall not be counted as Billable Tokens. All Billable Tokens shall be aggregated and reported monthly.

--- DRAFT CLAUSE B: Streaming-friendly meter (alternative) ---
Streaming Metering and Session Window: Streaming requests are counted in tokens. For customers electing the streaming-friendly meter, Redwood will apply a session-window smoothing mechanism that treats brief inactive intervals of less than thirty (30) seconds within an open session as continuous. Billing may be rounded according to the elected quantum: either (i) per-token; or (ii) per-second with a one (1) second quantum for billable seconds. For clarity, rounding per-second converts token-rate during the second into a billable token equivalent using the measured token rate at the server.

--- CARRY-FORWARD AND TRUE-UP ---
Carry-forward: For annual committed purchases, Customer may carry forward up to five percent (5%) of unused committed units from one monthly period to the immediately subsequent monthly period, provided the Customer maintains the annual commit. Any carry-forward amount shall be applied before any overage calculation. True-up: At the end of the quarter, actual usage in excess of committed units shall be invoiced at the overage rate specified in Appendix X.

--- WORKED EXAMPLE ---
Scenario: ACME streams conversational transcripts over 10,000 sessions in a month. Average tokens per session: 120. Total streamed tokens: 1,200,000.

- Under Clause A (per-token): billable tokens = 1,200,000 (minus any prefix cache deductions).
- Under Clause B (streaming-friendly), with session-window smoothing and per-second rounding (1s quantum), assume the server-measured average token rate is 5 tokens/sec. Rounding per second results in an effective 5 token/sec * total streamed seconds. If idle gaps <30s are merged, the total billed seconds decrease by 6% in this example, netting a billed token count of ~1,128,000.

Next steps: Laura and Karthik — if this looks good I can send a version to ACME legal with the attached term-sheet (redwood-billing-definitions-diff.txt) and the worked example. Jamie — if you prefer the streaming-friendly clause, let me know and we'll switch the term sheet to option B and mark the per-second quantum accordingly.

Regards,
Rishi
